source_audit_support.citation: Rational Method with SI conversion constant 0.00278; area-weighted runoff coefficient; PD 1096 NBC and RNPC pipe sizing tables.

proposed.text: A mixed-use development (1.8 hectares total, comprising 50% rooftop area with C = 0.85, 30% paved parking with C = 0.90, and 20% landscaped areas with C = 0.25) experiences a 10-year storm with intensity 140 mm/hr (per PD 1096 for the region). The developer proposes a 200 mm diameter storm drain at 0.75% slope (capacity ~0.050 m3/s per code tables). Will this pipe be sufficient, and why or why not?

options.text: No. The calculated discharge is approximately 0.522 m3/s, exceeding the pipe capacity of 0.050 m3/s by a factor of 10; a much larger diameter (450 mm or higher) is required.
Yes. The design discharge is less than 0.050 m3/s, so the 200 mm pipe is adequate and economical.
No. The landscape area has C = 0.25, which reduces total runoff below 0.050 m3/s; but water quality standards require a 300 mm pipe regardless.
Yes. Since this is a mixed-use site with some infiltration, the average coefficient is less than 0.60; the 200 mm pipe exceeds minimum requirements.

proposed.rationale: Step 1 - Weighted runoff coefficient (area-weighted): C = (0.50 x 0.85) + (0.30 x 0.90) + (0.20 x 0.25) = 0.425 + 0.27 + 0.05 = 0.745. Step 2 - Rational Method with SI conversion constant: Q (m3/s) = 0.00278 x C x I (mm/hr) x A (ha) = 0.00278 x 0.745 x 140 x 1.8 = 0.522 m3/s. Step 3 - Compare to pipe capacity: 0.522 m3/s vs 0.050 m3/s = factor of 10.4 exceedance. The 200 mm pipe is grossly undersized; correct answer is a. The original option a value of 0.0724 m3/s resulted from using C = 0.103 (erroneous: it appears the area fractions were multiplied twice or the landscaped C=0.25 dominated the weighting). Option b and d are incorrect because the weighted C of 0.745 is above 0.60 (not below). Option c is incorrect because the landscaped fraction (20%) is too small to reduce total runoff below 0.050 m3/s.
proposed.explanation: Mixed-use site runoff requires area-weighted C: C_w = Sum(A_i x C_i) / A_total = 0.745. Then Q = 0.00278 x C_w x I x A = 0.522 m3/s. The proposed 200 mm pipe (capacity 0.050 m3/s) is undersized by an order of magnitude.
